Messages from the club have separate jobs. Email goes through Gmail, texts go through Twilio, and card payments go through Stripe. We don't send email through Twilio, and we don't ask Stripe to send receipts.

Six kinds of email go through Gmail. Register receipts, online payment receipts, gift cards and indoor simulator confirmations go to customers. Pro shop activity alerts and server down alerts go to managers. Gmail allows about two thousand messages a day, so bulk marketing email would need a separate service.

All texts go through Twilio. That covers card approval texts, receipt texts, gift card texts and marketing campaigns. An approval text goes out once per payment. Numbers that replied STOP get no texts at all.

All texts come from one number, two four nine, eight zero five, zero five five six. It is the same club number shown on the website, and STOP or cancel replies arrive there too. The customer's number is found in order. First the number staff typed at the register, then the tee time player on the bill, then the first number on that booking, then the simulator booking. Online payments use the booking number.

Here is each payment type. Reader cards send an approval text automatically. Online tee times and simulator bookings send an approval text and an email receipt. Online memberships send only an email receipt. Keyed cards, cash, cheques and gift cards send nothing automatically, so staff send the receipt.

When a pro shop payment finishes, the Payment complete screen opens. The phone and email from the booking are already filled in. If the bill was paid only by reader card, the phone box stays empty because the approval text already went out. Staff can send it again after a wrong number or a repeat request.

Two things become automatic. Online payments send an email receipt within a minute of approval, so customers with a STOP number can still get one. Indoor simulator web bookings send a confirmation email. Keyed cards still need staff to send a receipt. Neither feature is live yet.
